why: Design previews with mock records (cards, domain forms, stickloop). app/preview/layout.tsx calls notFound() in production, so no person of any deployment reaches them.

The base starter workflow script, used only when this deployment keeps the customer-context and follow-ups specialists (STARTER_SCRIPT); a specialist is delegated to by its directory name, which never moves. A deployment that excludes either starts from a one-step script naming a specialist it has.
The agent API's Vercel project name in a `vercel env add` instruction: a person must type the name the project really has.

The generic agent package's real command names (its bin entries). A command a person copies must be one that exists; a deployment with its own package (npm run build:agent-cli) is shown that package's `login` / `mcp` instead.

literal: ^ first \(POST /api/ops/customers, or customer_create from the CLI\)\.$
why: The real API route and CLI command that create the record the error is about: renaming them in the message would send the caller to an endpoint that does not exist. The sentence around them is in the profile's words.
A request-validation error naming the API's own parameter, for a caller that omitted it. The UI always sends it, so a person using the UI never sees this.
A request-validation error listing the export API's accepted `type` values, for a caller that sent none. The UI always sends one.

The error renderAccountReport throws for an id outside the caller's workspace. It never reaches the report: the tool's error goes to the model, through the model-facing boundary that speaks it (check:agent-vocabulary), and the cross-workspace tests match it. Every label the reports print comes from the profile (reportWords).
The QuickJS prelude injected before a workflow script: code whose `data.customers()` / `data.deployments()` are the scripts' API, never shown to a person.

A code value, never a label: an enum value or record type (a TODO's containerType / linkType, a workflow's entity, an export `type`), a data-room tab or ops view key, a URL `?dataroom=` / `?view=` value, or an object key read by name. What a person reads for it comes from the profile (lib/ui-words.ts, domainView(...)).

A data-room domain's STORED name: the folder, its Master.xlsx and sheet, and the profile's dataroom.domains key are all named by it. Every place a person reads a domain shows its profile label instead (domainDisplay / domainLabel / sheetTitle / domainView(...).name). (One more "Deployments" in app/_components/dataroom.tsx is Vercel's own word on the Vercel connector card, "Syncs Deployments · Build logs · …": it names the third-party product's builds, not this product's record area.)

A key: a record field, API parameter or workbook column (customerId, customer_id, implementationStage, fdeOwner, rollout_id), a base tool name matched in a transcript (list_customers, get_customer), or a code property. Keys never move: the API, the database and the workbook key on them. Where a person reads one — a data-room sheet's header, a Markdown export's field — it is spoken through lib/ui-keys.ts (company_id, "Covering analyst").
An ops API route and its query parameter. Routes never move; the UI only fetches them.

An identifier: the customer-context specialist's directory name (delegated to by name, never translated; it is listed only when the profile keeps it), the stakeholders tab key, a stored enum value (customer-vpc), or a data-testid (impl-customer).
A localStorage / sessionStorage key. Renaming one would drop every person's saved chats, workspace and theme on the next load; a key is never shown.
A module export's or component's name, kept by the bundler in its module map. Never rendered.
A data-room tree node's id (a folder's id is its stored path) or a stored person type. The tree renders the node's name and its domain's profile label, never the id.

The translator's own table: the base words it maps FROM (BASE, PRODUCT_KEYS, the domain names). The UI imports it to recognise a model-facing tool name in a transcript (baseNameAmong) and to speak a key (lib/ui-keys.ts); none of these strings is rendered.

literal: ^(Deployments?|Implementations?|Rollouts?|Deployment id|Rollout id|Deployments, filtered by owner\.|Rollouts, filtered by owner\.)$
why: DEFAULT_DOMAINS: profiles/00-default.json's own labels for the two record areas, kept only so lib/profile-domains.ts can tell what a profile redefined. A relabelling profile overrides each of them, and the rendered pass shows none of them reaches a page.

blockerOwner's STORED value `Customer`, the key of the profile's option labels ({ "Customer": "Company" }). A person reads the label; the enum pass (1b) proves every visible enum value is shown through one.
A seed file's STORED path (dataroom.seed[].path): the folder in storage is Customers/. The data room shows it under the domain's label.
lib/ui-keys.ts's own table of which base words a KEY may carry: what it translates FROM, never rendered.
